rows.rationale: The clause applies to SRTPV systems over 17.5 kW, but the application is for a 45 kW system which should follow DSPV rules. | The clause is for HT installations over 150 kW, but this application is for a 45 kW LT installation.

The proposed solar capacity is 45.00 kWp, which is less than the 50kWp threshold mentioned in the clause. | The clause is related to the total capacity on the distribution transformer, but the proposed capacity does not exceed the 80% limit of the transformer's rated capacity.
The application's proposed solar capacity is 20 kW, which is not more than 20 kW, so the requirement for a check meter does not apply.

The cited clause specifies 0.2s class accuracy for main Solar Meters, but the application documents show both Solar Generation Meter and Net Meter are of 0.2S class accuracy, which is more stringent than required.
The application specifies 0.2S class meters, which are better than the 1.0 and 0.5S class required by the cited rule, but the rule does not support approving a higher class meter.
The clause does not apply to ground-mounted systems as per the amendment. | The specific clause governing the capacity of ground-mounted systems under GNM/VNM is missing.
The clause applies to systems over 50kWp, but the proposed system is 80kWp, so the decision is based on a lower threshold clause.
The cited clause is superseded by the 2025 amendment which allows changes twice a year with two months' notice.
The clause does not apply to ground-mounted systems, only rooftop.
The cited clause limits SLD waiver to 50 MW for BRPL, but the application is for a project that would exceed this limit.
The clause is from the Fifth Amendment Guidelines of 2024, but the application date is in 2026, and a later amendment may have superseded it.
The clause specifies a percentage that may be fixed by the Commission, but does not provide a specific percentage limit like 15% or 75%.
The cited clause does not apply to ground-mounted systems, which is the case here. | The applicable clause for ground-mounted systems is not cited.
The clause specifies capacity limits for Renewable Energy Systems under Group Net Metering or Virtual Net Metering, but does not address the minimum capacity requirement of 5 kW.

The clause is superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-3.2, which came into effect on 2026-01-20. | The clause does not apply to the application as it pertains to reporting requirements for distribution licensees, not the eligibility of consumers for VNM.

The clause applies to residential consumers and MSME (Manufacturing) Enterprises, but the application is for an HTP-I Industrial tariff category. | Clause 6.2c-ii applies to projects under REC Mechanism for captive use, which is not the case here.
The application is for a 30 kW system, which is below the 50 kW threshold mentioned in the clause.
The decision states the cumulative capacity can exceed the distribution transformer's capacity, but the cited clause limits it to the transformer's capacity.
The clause applies to DSPV systems of capacity more than 50kWp, not SRTPV systems of capacity more than 17.5kW.
The clause is outdated and superseded by newer regulations. | The clause does not apply to the meter accuracy requirement for main Solar Meters.
The application proposes a 10.00 kWp system, but the sanctioned load is 8.0 kW, exceeding the 100% limit.
The clause does not apply as the application is for net billing, not net feed-in, and the sanctioned load is 8 kW while the proposed system is 10 kW.
The application is for commercial shops, not covered under the cited clause for hospitals, colleges, etc.
The clause is from 2024, but a later amendment in 2025 (DL-C3-015) may supersede it.

The application is for an MSME (Manufacturing) Enterprise, not a residential consumer or captive consumer. | Clause 6.2c-ii does not apply to MSME (Manufacturing) Enterprises, only to projects under Third Party Sale or REC Mechanism.
The clause does not apply as the proposed solar capacity exceeds the sanctioned load.
The cited clause is superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-9.2b, which allows for two changes in a financial year with an advance notice of two months.
The clause is not in force as the application was submitted on 2026-03-30, after the October 2024 deadline.
The clause is not in force as it was effective on 2024-06-07, after the claim was received on 2026-02-16.
The cumulative capacity for TPDDL has already exceeded 110 MW, making the waiver inapplicable.
The clause is superseded by GJ-C3-003#cl-13.5-class, which is more recent and applicable.
The clause is not in force as it is dated 2024-06-07, after the application date of 2026-02-14.
The clause is superseded by a later amendment effective 2026-01-20. | The clause is superseded by a later amendment effective 2026-01-20.
